annotations.title: Ski and snowshoe tours at a place

description: Ski and snowshoe tours in the Alps at a place: the routes up to a summit, hut or pass, and the routes that start in a valley or at a hut. Each with title, grade in the scale of the language, elevation gain, length, and the start seen from the place. From the guidebook and portal data shown in the topo^alpin app; not current conditions. Say the grade, the elevation gain, where the route starts and who gave the grade: gradeSource on each tour, explained once in gradeSources; a grade with ~ is estimated by topo^alpin. Give each tour with its appUrl, which opens it in the topo^alpin app. Say where each route in startingHere starts: it can lie in another valley, across a pass. Where target.endBelowM is above 30, the line ends at a ski depot that far below the summit and the rest is not in the route: say so. Pass on the field notice, check avalanche_bulletin for the tour, and use tour_terrain for how steep it is and how much lies in avalanche terrain.

discipline.description: Only ski or only snowshoe tours. Default both.

lang.description: Language for titles and grades. Default en.

lat.description: Latitude, WGS 84. topo^alpin covers the Alps only.

limit.description: How many tours per list. Default 10.

placeId.description: When query matched several places, the placeId of the one the user means, from that list. Give it together with the same query.

query.description: Name of a summit, hut, pass or town.

radiusKm.description: How far a start in startingHere may lie from the place; routes up to it count wherever they start. Default 5.

name: winter_tours

appUrl.description: Opens this place in the topo^alpin app.

dataStale.description: True: the data is older than its source is refreshed, or the source reports a fault. Say that it may be outdated. null: unknown, not fresh.

dataUpdatedAt.description: When the data behind this answer was produced (ISO 8601, UTC; a date for a fixed release). With several sources, the oldest. null: unknown.

disclaimer.description: Automatic and possibly outdated. Pass it on.

elevationSource.description: Where elevationM comes from: input (given), place (of the place found) or terrain (our terrain model at the point). null: no elevation known.

accuracy.description: Only for estimate: how close the estimate came to grades from authors.

gradeSources.description: Each gradeSource in this answer, once: who gives the grade. Pass it on with the grades.

missing.description: Present where there is no tour. Pass it on.

more.description: Present where limit cut the list: there are more. Say so, or call again.

notice.description: Pass this on with the tours.

alternatives.description: Other places or areas the query may mean, each with how to ask for it: the same query with its placeId, lat and lon, or query.

label.description: Check it: a wrong place gives wrong tours.

partialMatch.description: No place has the name asked for; this one has a longer name that contains it. Name the place you used, and ask the user if they may mean another.

type.description: peak, saddle, alpine_hut, wilderness_hut, shelter, tour_place (where our tours start or end), town, or point where lat and lon were given.

radiusKm.description: How far a start in startingHere may lie from the place.

sources.description: Name these when using the data.

startingHere.description: Routes that start within radiusKm of the place in a straight line, nearest first; a start can lie in another valley, across a pass. Say where it starts. Empty at a summit.

appUrl.description: Opens this tour in the topo^alpin app, on the map. Give it to the user with the tour.

grade.description: SAC scale for ski, WT for snowshoe, in the scale of the language. ~ means estimated.

gradeEstimated.description: true: estimated from the terrain, not given by an author.

gradeSource.description: Who gave the grade: SAC, Petzl, Panico, Alpenverein, or estimate. See gradeSources.

normalRoute.description: Whether the source lists it as the normal route. Only the SAC does; null elsewhere means unknown, not that it is none.

role.description: A descent is its own route, from the summit down.

start.description: Where the route starts, seen from the place.

distanceKm.description: In a straight line from the place.

summit.description: The goal: summit, pass or hut.

elevationM.description: Of the summit, pass or hut; a summit at its top.

endBelowM.description: How far below the summit the line ends; above 30 at a ski depot, the rest is not in the line. null for a pass or hut.

target.description: The goal of the route as topo^alpin determined it from the terrain; its name is summit. null where it is not known.

aspectsSteep.description: Aspects of the slopes of 30 degrees or more along the line, on skis and on foot.

items.description: Compass direction: N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW.

atesMax.description: Highest ATES class along the whole route, on foot too, 0 to 4; null where none was assessed.

onFoot.description: The part on foot above a ski depot, often the steepest: name it with the grade. null: there is none.

steepM.description: Metres on skis at 30 degrees or more.

steepestDeg.description: Steepest point on skis only, in degrees, held over 20 m of height: a part on foot above a ski depot is not in it, and is often steeper; it stands in onFoot, and tour_terrain shows it in detail. See terrainExplained.

terrain.description: The terrain in brief; null where there is no terrain data: unknown, not flat.

terrainExplained.description: What the terrain values mean, once per answer. Explain them when you name them.

toSummit.description: Routes up to the place, ascents first, then descents from it: they end within 1 km of it, wherever they start. radiusKm does not apply to them.
